newsitem.title: USA: LTV to buy United Dominion unit for $187.5 million.
newsitem.headline: LTV to buy United Dominion unit for $187.5 million.

text.p: LTV Corp. said Wednesday it was making three major investments in steel fabrication and manufacturing businesses in the United States and overseas, including a deal worth about $188 million.
LTV said it agreed to buy the Varco-Pruden Buildings unit from United Dominion Industries Inc. for $187.5 million in cash.

Varco-Pruden, based in Memphis, Tenn., makes low-rise steel building systems for manufacturing, warehousing, school and commercial applications. It operates eight U.S. factories and has joint venture manufacturing facilities in China, Brazil and Argentina. Revenues were $305 million in 1996.
The deal is subject to regulatory approval and the completion of definitive agreements.
LTV also said it has acquired a 25 percent stake in Lagermex SA de CV, which is building an $18.5 million automotive steel processing operation in Puebla, Mexico. Terms were not disclosed.
Lagermax will be the sole domestic source of automotive blanks, or pieces of steel prepared for stamping into body parts, for Volkswagen de Mexico. Operations will begin in fall 1997.

LTV said its third investment was through an equity stake in the TWB Co. LLC, a joint venture of Thyssen Stahl, and Worthington Industries Inc. TWB is a supplier of tailored, laser-welded steel blanks to the domestic auto industry.
LTV did not disclose the size of the stake or the price.
LTV stock rose 12.5 cents to $13.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
